parts.title: UPSC Economy: Money & Capital Markets
parts.intro: Today we study the 'Engine of Investment'. The financial market is where those with surplus funds (investors) meet those who need funds (corporates/govt). We explore the 'Money Market' (short-term) and the 'Capital Market' (long-term/Stock market). For UPSC, focus on 'Financial Instruments' like T-Bills, Commercial Papers, and the role of 'SEBI'. Let's master the language of the stock exchange today.

pages.title: Money Market
pages.intro: Market for short-term funds (≤1 year), regulated by RBI, dealing in T-Bills, Commercial Paper, and Certificates of Deposit.

items.label: Treasury Bills (T-Bills)
items.value: Issued by Govt. of India; safest short-term borrowing instrument.

items.label: Commercial Paper
items.value: Short-term loan issued by large companies to raise quick funds.

items.label: Certificates of Deposit (CDs)
items.value: Issued by banks for fixed short-period deposits.

pages.title: Capital Market
pages.intro: Market for long-term funds (>1 year), regulated by SEBI, comprising Primary and Secondary Markets.

pages.title: Equity vs Debt
pages.intro: Equity means ownership with variable returns; Debt means lending with fixed interest and no ownership.

pages.title: SEBI (Securities & Exchange Board of India)
pages.intro: Statutory body established in 1992 to protect investors and regulate stock exchanges and mutual funds.

branches.label: Powers
branches.value: Make rules, punish fraud & insider trading

pages.title: FDI vs FPI
pages.intro: FDI is long-term with management control; FPI is short-term passive investment in financial assets.

cards.front: Which institution regulates the Money Market?
What is the primary duration of funds in the Money Market?
cards.back: Short-term funds, typically less than one year.

cards.front: Which institution regulates the Capital Market?
cards.back: The Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI).

cards.front: What is the purpose of the Primary Market?
cards.back: To sell new securities for the first time, such as through an IPO.

cards.front: What is the main difference between Equity and Debt investments?
cards.back: Equity represents ownership in a company with variable returns, while Debt represents a loan with fixed interest.

cards.front: When was SEBI established as a statutory body?
What are the two main entities regulated by SEBI?
What distinguishes FDI from FPI regarding management control?
cards.back: FDI involves management control, whereas FPI is a passive investment without control.

cards.front: Why is FPI often referred to as 'hot money'?
cards.back: Because it is a short-term investment that can be quickly moved out of a country.
